```{r}
#| include: false
library(apaTables)
```

## Method

This paragraph is body text before anything else, so the document has at
least one ordinary portrait page ahead of the rotated table.

## Results

@fig-scatter shows a figure. It exists so the document is structurally
capable of exposing a header-relationship-ID shift -- a bare table-only
fixture cannot (D31): pandoc allocates new relationship IDs above the
reference document's own header/footer IDs in the order things are added to
the document, so a fixture with nothing BUT a table cannot tell a correct,
hardcoded rId8/rId9/rId12 apart from one that happened to be right only
because nothing else claimed a relationship first.

```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "A Scatterplot"
#| echo: false
plot(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
```

@tbl-wide is wide enough that apaTables' layout ladder rotates it onto a
landscape page rather than shrinking its type (D7, rotate before shrink).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-wide
#| tbl-cap: "Motor Trend Car Road Tests: Correlations"
#| echo: false
apaTables:::apa_quarto_markdown_block(apa.cor.table(mtcars))
```

This paragraph is body text after the rotated table, on whatever page
follows it.
